arxiv-1412-6395.title: SClib, a hack for straightforward embedded C functions in Python
arxiv-1412-6395.creator: Esteban Fuentes, Hector E. Martinez
arxiv-1412-6395.description: Abstract We present SClib, a simple hack that allows easy and straightforward evaluation of C functions within Python code, boosting flexibility for better trade-off between computation power and feature availability, such as visualization and existing computation routines in SciPy. We also present two cases were SClib has been used.

arxiv-2204-11980.title: Decentralisation Conscious Players And System Reliability
arxiv-2204-11980.creator: Sarah Azouvi, Alexander Hicks
arxiv-2204-11980.description: Abstract We propose a game-theoretic model of the reliability of decentralised systems based on Varian’s model of system reliability [ 27 ] , to which we add a new normalised total effort case that models decentralisation conscious players who prioritise decentralisation. We derive the Nash equilibria in the normalised total effort game.

arxiv-2210-09146.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Self-Duality Symmetries. We study how non-invertible self-duality defects arise in theories with a holographic dual. We focus on the paradigmatic example of 𝔰 ​ 𝔲 ​ ( N ) \mathfrak{su}(N) 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 SYM. arxiv-2301-08902.title: Reacceleration of Galactic Cosmic Rays Beyond the Knee at the Termination Shock of a Cosmic-Ray-Driven Galactic Wind
arxiv-2301-08902.creator: Payel Mukhopadhyay, Enrico Peretti, Noémie Globus, Paul Simeon, Roger Blandford
arxiv-2301-08902.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Payel Mukhopadhyay, Enrico Peretti, Noémie Globus, Paul Simeon, Roger Blandford. The origin of cosmic rays above the knee in the spectrum is an unsolved problem. We present a wind model in which interstellar gas flows along a non-rotating, expanding flux tube with a changing speed and cross-sectional area. Cosmic rays from Galactic sources, such as supernova remnants, which are coupled to the plasma via Alfvén waves, provide the main pressure source for driving this outflow.

arxiv-2307-05073.title: Knowledge-wh and False Belief Sensitivity: A Logical Study (An Extended Abstract)
arxiv-2307-05073.creator: Yuanzhe Yang
arxiv-2307-05073.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yuanzhe Yang. In epistemic logic, a way to deal with knowledge-wh is to interpret them as a kind of mention-some knowledge (MS-knowledge). But philosophers and linguists have challenged both the sufficiency and necessity of such an account: some argue that knowledge-wh has, in addition to MS-knowledge, also a sensitivity to false belief (FS); others argue that knowledge-wh might only imply mention-some true belief (MS-true belief). In this paper, we offer a logical study for all these different accounts.

arxiv-2308-03209.title: Communication-Free Distributed GNN Training with Vertex Cut
arxiv-2308-03209.creator: Kaidi Cao, Rui Deng, Shirley Wu, Edward W Huang, Karthik Subbian, Jure Leskovec
arxiv-2308-03209.description: Abstract Training Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) on real-world graphs consisting of billions of nodes and edges is quite challenging, primarily due to the substantial memory needed to store the graph and its intermediate node and edge features, and there is a pressing need to speed up the training process.

arxiv-2311-00040.title: How does the presence of bar affects the fueling of supermassive black holes ? An IllustrisTNG100 perspective 2015 How does the presence of bar affects the fueling of supermassive black holes ? An IllustrisTNG100 perspective – References
arxiv-2311-00040.creator: Sandeep Kumar Kataria & M. Vivek
arxiv-2311-00040.description: Abstract We conduct a statistical study of black hole masses of barred and unbarred galaxies in the IllustrisTNG100 cosmological magneto-hydrodynamical simulations. This work aims to understand the role of the bars in the growth of central supermassive black hole mass and its implications on AGN fueling.

arxiv-2410-01427.title: Regularized e-processes: anytime valid inference with knowledge-based efficiency gains
arxiv-2410-01427.creator: Ryan Martin
arxiv-2410-01427.description: Abstract Classical statistical methods have theoretical justification when the sample size is predetermined. In applications, however, it’s often the case that sample sizes are data-dependent rather than predetermined. The aforementioned methods aren’t reliable in this latter case, hence the recent interest in e-processes and methods that are anytime valid, i.e., reliable for any dynamic data-collection plan.

arxiv-2411-11423.title: TeeMate : Fast and Efficient Confidential Container using Shared Enclave 1264 Thanks: † \dagger These authors contributed equally to this work.
arxiv-2411-11423.creator: Chulmin Lee † \dagger, Jaewon Hur † \dagger, Sangho Lee, Byoungyoung Lee
arxiv-2411-11423.description: Abstract . Confidential container is becoming increasingly popular as it meets both needs for efficient resource management by cloud providers, and data protection by cloud users. Specifically, confidential containers integrate the container and the enclave, aiming to inherit the design-wise advantages of both—i.e., resource management and data protection.

arxiv-2412-10108.title: Spectral analysis of metamaterials in curved manifolds
arxiv-2412-10108.creator: Tomáš Faikl
arxiv-2412-10108.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tomáš Faikl. Negative-index metamaterials possess a negative refractive index and thus present an interesting substance for designing uncommon optical effects such as invisibility cloaking. This paper deals with operators encountered in an operator-theoretic description of metamaterials. First, we introduce an indefinite Laplacian and consider it on a compact tubular neighbourhood in constantly curved compact two-dimensional Riemannian ambient manifolds, with Euclidean rectangle in ℝ 2 \mathbb{R}^{2} being present as a special case. As this operator is not semi-bounded, standard form-theoretic methods cannot be applied.

arxiv-2503-14208.title: The EXOD search for faint transients in XMM-Newton observations
arxiv-2503-14208.creator: N. Khan, E. Quintin, N. A. Webb, R. Webbe, M. Gupta, I. Pastor-Marazuela, F. Castellani, A. D. Schwope, I. Traulsen, A. Nebot
arxiv-2503-14208.description: Abstract Context. The XMM-Newton observatory has accumulated a vast archive of over 17,000 X-ray observations over the last 25 years. However, the standard data processing pipelines may fail to detect certain types of transient X-ray sources due to their short-lived or dim nature.

britannica-1911-faber-basil.title: Faber, Basil (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-faber-basil.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-faber-basil.description: Article 'Faber, Basil' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 10), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. theologian, was born at Sorau, in lower Lusatia, in 1520. In 1538 he entered the university of Wittenberg, studying as pauper gratis under Melanchthon. Choosing the schoolmaster’s profession, he became successively rector of the schools at Nordhausen, Tennstadt (1555), Magdeburg (1557) and Quedlinburg (1560). From this last post he was removed in December 1570 as a Crypto-Calvinist.

pmc-10589940.title: Re-stratification of patients with copy-number low endometrial cancer by clinicopathological characteristics
pmc-10589940.creator: Li Liwei, Li He, Dai Yibo, Zhao Luyang, Shen Zhihui, Kang Nan, Shen Danhua, Wang Junzhu, Wang Zhiqi, Wang Jianliu
pmc-10589940.description: ObjectiveTo stratify patients with copy-number low (CNL) endometrial cancer (EC) by clinicopathological characteristics.MethodsEC patients who underwent surgery between June 2018 and June 2022 at Peking University People’s Hospital were included and further classified according to TCGA molecular subtyping: POLE ultramutated, microsatellite instability high (MSI-H), CNL, and copy-number high (CNH). Clinicopathological characteristics and prognosis of CNL patients were retrospectively reviewed.

pmc-11510107.title: A Scalable Method to Fabricate 2D Hydrogel Substrates for Mechanobiology Studies with Independent Tuning of Adhesiveness and Stiffness
pmc-11510107.creator: Alessandro Gandin, Veronica Torresan, Tito Panciera, Giovanna Brusatin
pmc-11510107.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Mechanical signals from the extracellular matrix are crucial in guiding cellular behavior. Two-dimensional hydrogel substrates for cell cultures serve as exceptional tools for mechanobiology studies because they mimic the biomechanical and adhesive characteristics of natural environments. However, the interdisciplinary knowledge required to synthetize and manipulate these biomaterials typically restricts their widespread use in biological laboratories, which may not have the material science expertise or specialized instrumentation.

pmc-11710264.title: The role of clusterin and the variant rs11136000_T throughout the spectrum of Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11710264.creator: Marina Tedeschi Dauar, Cynthia Picard, Anne Labonte, Sylvia Villeneuve, Judes Poirier, PREVENT‐AD Research Group
pmc-11710264.description: BackgroundClusterin is a major cholesterol transporter in the central nervous system (CNS) and different SNPs in the CLU gene have been associated with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) risk. The rs11136000_T variant in the CLU gene has been shown to decrease the risk of AD.

pmc-12451856.description: with Horst Korf in August 2023. Photograph taken by Beate Korf. Morten Møller was born in Odense, Denmark on November 29, 1942. pmc-12511288.title: Understanding dating intentions on linkedin through perceived trustworthiness and user engagement
pmc-12511288.creator: Mohamed Ben Arbia, Myriam Ertz, Aws Horrich, Rym Bouzaabia
pmc-12511288.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The fast expansion of social media reshapes interpersonal communication, networking, and identity expression uniquely. The research explores LinkedIn’s repurpose as a platform for dating intentions, challenging its conventional use as a professional networking site. By analyzing data from 331 LinkedIn users with dating intentions surveyed via an online questionnaire, the study unveils how perceived trustworthiness, safety, self-presentation, engagement behaviors, social validation, and self-confidence impact romantic pursuits. The findings suggest that trustworthiness enhances safety perceptions, which subsequently foster dating intent.

pmc-12657610.title: Oncoplastic surgery for cutaneous head and neck cancers: A novel technique combining wide excision, local flap reconstruction and sentinel node biopsy
pmc-12657610.creator: Caroline A. Gjorup, Michael Chae, Terence Wong, David J. Coker, Thomas E. Pennington
pmc-12657610.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and purposesSentinel node biopsy (SNB) procedures in the head and neck (H&N) region can be technically demanding due to anatomic and size constraints. Often, node procurement is attempted through small incisions, making identification of crucial anatomy difficult.

pmc-12994049.title: Comparison of conventional formulas and machine learning models for estimating serum low-density lipoprotein cholesterol
pmc-12994049.creator: Ruqiya Al Dhuhli, Nafila Al Riyami, Fatma Al Farsi, Ali Al Khamyasi, Huda Al Saadi, Said Al Alawi, Qutaiba Alfarai, Hamza Zidoum, Faisal Alsalmani, Yousef Almarshodi, Fahad Zadjali
pmc-12994049.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAccurate estimation of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is essential for cardiovascular risk assessment and monitoring. Because β-quantification is labor-intensive and impractical for routine use, several equations have been developed to estimate LDL-C indirectly, including the widely used Friedewald formula.

pmc-13385008.title: Preoperative gap phenotypes in functionally aligned robotic total knee arthroplasty: derivation and internal coherence of a driver-based classification
pmc-13385008.creator: Eduardo Frois Temponi, Jared Philip Sachs, Matheus Braga Jacques Gonçalves, Luiz Fernando Machado Soares, Lúcio Honório de Carvalho Júnior
pmc-13385008.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Robotic total knee arthroplasty (TKA) enables repeated intraoperative quantification of preoperative alignment, flexion deformity, and medial and lateral compartment gaps in extension and at 90° flexion before component positioning, but the preoperative patterns guiding functional-alignment planning remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to derive a pragmatic driver-based classification from preoperative robotic data and evaluate its internal coherence across the surgical workflow. We analyzed 68 consecutive primary functionally aligned robotic TKAs performed by a single surgeon using a CT-based robotic-arm platform.

pmc-13536761.title: Understanding occupational self-efficacy for health and meaningfulness at work: a qualitative study among home care workers with threatened work ability
pmc-13536761.creator: Stina Wallin, Linda Estman, Malin Andtfolk
pmc-13536761.description: BackgroundRetaining home care workers who are experiencing increasing job demands alongside deteriorating occupational health has become a growing concern. Previous research has found occupational self-efficacy, that is belief in one’s own capabilities to successfully fulfil work-related responsibilities, associated with work wellbeing and meaningfulness.
